title: Tool-call arguments cut off by the output token limit
summary: The model stops at the output token limit partway through the arguments of a tool call.

messages.content: Create an event for a weekend pottery workshop in Málaga on 2026-11-14 with 30 attendees. Invent their full names, mixing Spanish, Greek and Japanese names written in their own scripts.
Create a catalog of 30 flowering plants for a greenhouse. Include an accented Latin, Greek or Japanese common name for each plant and a short description of its flowers.

requirements.text: Partial tool-call arguments are never presented as a complete parsed call.
The caller can tell that the output stopped at the token limit.

grading_notes: Where supported, effort none disables reasoning to reserve the limit for tool arguments. Returning unparsed partial arguments satisfies the first requirement; the caller must also be told that the output stopped at the token limit. Repairing the arguments into a complete parsed call contradicts what the wire carried. Ollama providers are not listed because they emit whole calls or no call at the token limit, so the partial-argument requirement cannot be exercised. Gemini uses a botanical catalog override. Its functionCall args are objects, so a token limit may yield no call; the partial-argument check is then vacuous, while truncation signalling is still required. MINIMAL may spend tokens on thoughts. Recordings must establish the actual MAX_TOKENS shape.
